q: What is the recommended fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) for a supermarket with a PCC of ₱50 million or less?
n: Supermarkets are Group 2 buildings (moderate complexity). For PCC of ₱50 million or less the recommended DAEDS fee is 6%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2.

q: What is the most common way architects are paid?
n: Architects are most commonly paid a percentage of the project construction cost. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (methods of compensation).

q: Which method bills by the hour, day or month?
n: The time basis method bills by the hour, day or month (per diem). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: Which method suits a scope that is clearly and fully defined?
n: A lump sum (fixed fee) suits a scope that is clearly and fully defined in advance. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: What is the DAEDS for a mall?
n: Malls and mall complexes are Group 2 buildings. For PCC of ₱50 million or less the recommended DAEDS fee is 6% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2.

q: What is the DAEDS for an auditorium?
n: Auditoriums are Group 3 buildings (exceptional character and complexity). For PCC of ₱50 million or less the recommended DAEDS fee is 7% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3.

q: What is the DAEDS for a parking structure?
n: Parking structures are Group 1 buildings (simplest utilization). For PCC of ₱50 million or less the recommended DAEDS fee is 5% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.1.

q: How is an ocular inspection usually paid?
o: Per diem or honorarium plus reimbursable expenses
n: Short engagements such as an ocular inspection are paid per diem or as an honorarium, plus reimbursable expenses. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (methods of compensation).

q: Under the Architect's Guidelines, what is the minimum recommended fee for post-construction services (value pricing, as a percentage of gross rental)?
n: The recommended fee for post-construction services under value-pricing is 4% to 6% of gross rental, so the minimum is 4%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: Maximum remuneration under Post Construction services.
n: The value-pricing range for post-construction services is 4% to 6% of gross rental, so the maximum is 6%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: Mode of payment for post-construction services.
n: An architect doing post-construction services (building administrator or property manager) may be paid a monthly salary or fee. That is one of the listed methods, with value-pricing, MDPE, retainer and professional fee plus expenses. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.

q: Under regular design services, what share of the fee is paid on signing the contract?
n: On signing the service agreement, the owner pays 5% of the professional fee as the engagement (mobilization) fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.1.

q: Contract documents percentage of payment.
n: The contract documents phase is paid 50% of the fee, bringing cumulative payments to 90%. The schedule is 5% on signing, 15% schematic, 20% design development, 50% contract documents and 10% construction. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: The architect's staff and consultants' fees are part of what cost?
n: The salaries of the architect's staff and the fees of consultants on a project are direct costs (direct personnel and project expenses). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (MDPE).

q: DAEDS Residential.
n: Residences are Group 4. The recommended DAEDS fee is 10% of PCC (6% for DADS). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: RPF for DAEDS for the first unit of a residential project.
n: In a housing project, the first residential unit is charged the full Group 4 rate of 10% of PCC for DAEDS. Added units are charged reduced percentages. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Group 7.

q: DAEDS Monumental
n: Monumental buildings (memorials, museums, mausoleums) are Group 5. The recommended DAEDS fee is 12% of PCC (7.5% for DADS). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5.

q: Post-construction service is compensated based on.
n: Value-pricing for post-construction services is an incentive-type fee: a percentage of gross rental (4–6%) that rewards efficient operation, effectively a percentage plus performance bonus. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: What is the lower limit of the recommended post-construction services fee, as a percentage of gross rental?
n: The recommended value-pricing fee for post-construction services is 4% to 6% of gross rental, with a lower limit of 4%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: What is the upper limit of the recommended post-construction services fee, as a percentage of gross rental?
n: The recommended value-pricing fee for post-construction services is 4% to 6% of gross rental, with an upper limit of 6%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.

q: How much percentage of the total cost will an owner pay to the architect after completing the contract document phase?
n: Cumulative payments after the contract documents phase are 5% + 15% + 20% + 50% = 90% of the fee. The last 10% is paid during construction. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Which method pays the architect a set amount at regular intervals?
n: A retainer pays the architect a set amount at regular intervals to keep his services available. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: Which pricing ties the fee to measurable revenue or profit the project brings the client?
n: Value-based pricing ties the fee to the measurable value, revenue or profit the project brings the client. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205 (value-pricing).

q: Manner of payment for incentive-based Construction Management Contracting Concept (Price Adjustment Provisions).
n: Under the incentive-based construction management concept, the architect-CM is paid as a percentage of work progress, with price adjustment provisions. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 208 (Construction Management Services).

q: DAEDS stands for:
o: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services
Development Architectural and Engineering Design Services
n: DAEDS means Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services: architecture plus the allied engineering disciplines. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: DADS stands for:
n: DADS means Detailed Architectural Design Services, architecture only, without the engineering disciplines. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: The New Methods of Compensation, which form part of the Standards of Professional Practice, were approved by the Professional Board of Architecture (PRBOA) and took effect in:
n: The new methods of compensation in the SPP were approved by the PRBOA and took effect in 2016, published in the Official Gazette of 19 September 2016. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (Official Gazette Vol. 112 No. 38).

q: The architect can estimate project construction cost by all of these EXCEPT:
n: Construction cost can be estimated by the area method, volume method or detailed estimate. "Interest rate method" is not an estimating method. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: Which estimating technique suits project definition and schematic design?
n: The area (cost per m²) method gives quick estimates at project definition and schematic design, before quantities exist. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate; RSMeans Square Foot Costs.

q: What is the cost of the completed building to the owner, including structure, MEPF and all elements designed by the architect?
n: Project construction cost is the cost of the completed building to the owner, including structure, MEPF and all elements designed by the architect. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (definitions).

q: If the client elects not to include the allied engineers’ services on the architect's contract, who will be the overall coordinator of the engineers’ work?
n: Even if the client contracts the engineers separately, the architect remains the overall coordinator of the engineers' work as prime professional. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: For simple projects under the New Methods of Compensation under the Standards of Professional Practice, how much will be charged if the project is less than 50M?
n: Simple projects are Group 1. For PCC of ₱50 million or less the recommended DAEDS fee is 5%. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.1.

q: An architect was commissioned to design a Residential Project under Detailed Architectural Design Service (DADS). What is the professional fee of the architect if the project cost is Ten Million pesos?
n: A residence is Group 4. The DADS fee is 6% of PCC: 0.06 × ₱10,000,000 = ₱600,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: The client eventually decided to award and include Engineering disciplines to the firm. What professional fee should the firm now charge?
n: With engineering added, the service becomes DAEDS at 10% of PCC for Group 4: 0.10 × ₱10,000,000 = ₱1,000,000. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: Which cost includes construction plus all professional fees and permits?
n: Project development cost covers construction plus all professional fees, permits and other project costs (land, financing). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (definitions).

q: In project development, professional and permit fees are:
n: Professional and permit fees are soft costs, project costs that are not physical construction. Source: RSMeans; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: Who pays for a professional's insurance during a project?
n: Project-specific professional liability insurance required by the owner is a cost the owner pays, as a reimbursable expense. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (reimbursable expenses).

q: An architect was commissioned by a friend to design a townhouse project. The architect was specifically asked to prepare feasibility studies and marketing posters for the project. What type of compensation should the architect receive?
n: Feasibility studies and marketing posters are non-creative, time-based work, best compensated by a multiple of direct personnel expenses. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201 and 202 (MDPE).
